                            THE PRESIDENT:    The invocation

                 today will be given by Dr. Ronald W. Steward,

                 Pastor of Union Missionary Baptist Church in

                 Albany.

                            REVEREND STEWARD:    Let us pray.

                 Heavenly Father, the greatest gift of freedom

                 is the right to be ones' true self.  For true

                 freedom is where people find peace through

                 justice.

                            We intend today in this prayer to

                 ask Your blessings upon this assembly, to

                 furnish each individual with the means where

                 they can enact legislation that will be

                 beneficial to all of us in this, our State.

                            In these days many prejudices and

                 mass evils scar the tissues of our human life.

                 There are still multitudes of impoverished

                 men, woman and children who are forced to

                 forget the inherent dignity or to give up





                                                          1628



                 efforts to secure recognition of their rights

                 by others.

                            As individuals in the economic and

                 political communities, O Lord, they are made

                 to count or nothing, subject to forces where

                 they are denied the power to develop their

                 potentials.  These brothers of ours never

                 become all that they might be, reflecting Your

                 glory in their freedom.

                            May these men and women be granted

                 the courage today and fearlessness to fight

                 against evil to make no peace with oppression.

                 May they reverently use their office,

                 employing it in the pursuit of justice and

                 right among mankind.

                            These and other blessings we ask to

                 the glory of Your holy name.

                            Amen.

                            THE SECRETARY:    Senator Stafford

                 from the Committee on Finance reports the

                 following nominations:

                            As a member of the Public Service

                 Commission, Leonard A. Weiss of Albany.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Skelos.





                                                          1635



                            SENATOR SKELOS:    Move the

                 nomination, please.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Breslin.

                            SENATOR BRESLIN:    Thank you,

                 Madam President.

                            I would like to briefly second the

                 nomination of Leonard Weiss, whose practiced

                 law in our area for over 50 years.

                            Judge Weiss is a distinguished

                 practicing lawyer who was appointed a City

                 Court judge and rose to be the presiding judge

                 of the Appellate Division, Third Department,

                 as well as an acting Court of Appeals judge.

                            Upon leaving the bench and in

                 preparation for the Public Service Commission

                 he has been doing public service locally in

                 our area for the last several years, assisting

                 people who sought offices for government.

                            It is truly a wonderful appointment

                 by our Governor to elevate Judge Weiss to the

                 Public Service Commission.

                            Thank you, Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Wright.

                            SENATOR WRIGHT:    Thank you, Madam

                 President.





                                                          1636



                            It is also my honor to rise and

                 second the nomination for confirmation of

                 Judge Weiss.  As has been pointed out, the

                 judge has been appointed by first Governor

                 Carey and then Governor Cuomo and now we're

                 very pleased to join with Governor Pataki in

                 moving the nomination and confirmation of the

                 Judge as a member of the Public Service

                 Commission.

                            Truly the Judge brings a judicial

                 background and temperament that will be

                 beneficial to the deliberations of the Public

                 Service Commission and more importantly brings

                 years of public and civic service to the

                 people of this State and the people of this

                 community.

                            I too rise in a bipartisan effort

                 to recommend the confirmation of Judge Weiss.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Hoffmann.

                            SENATOR HOFFMANN:    I too am

                 delighted to rise and second the nomination of

                 Judge Weiss as a new member of the Public

                 Service Commission.

                            My friendship with him has been

                 over the last few years since I have been a





                                                          1637



                 member of this body in Albany.  But I know

                 that his commitment to public service goes

                 back virtually his entire life.  In fact, he

                 had the unique experience as a young man of

                 having served in the CCC, the Civilian

                 Conservation Corps.  One of the pioneers in

                 this country who helped us through some of

                 this nations darkest days.

                            While he serves on the Public

                 Service Commission I am confident that Judge

                 Weiss will remember what life was like for

                 people when they struggled through the

                 depression and how they found great difficulty

                 in meeting their most essential expenses.  And

                 he will remember when he is looking at

                 requests for rate increases and adjustments in

                 the costs at the very highest end of the

                 spectrum in the utility field that it is the

                 people at the very lowest level who will

                 ultimately bear the greatest burden.

                            I am confident that the Public

                 Service Commission is in good hands with Judge

                 Weiss as a new member.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Gentile.

                            SENATOR GENTILE:    Madam





                                                          1638



                 President, I wish to speak on the nomination.

                            While I don't personally know Mr.

                 Weiss, I have heard many great things about

                 him from my colleagues who have worked with

                 him here in Albany, and from what I hear on

                 the floor today.  However, there is one

                 troubling aspect of this nomination that

                 concerns me and it has come to my attention

                 that Mr. Weiss, upon taking his role at the

                 Public Service Commission will not only

                 receive a salary, but also continue to receive

                 his pension from his previous government

                 service.

                            That is a practice that I have been

                 opposed to.  That is a practice I have spoken

                 out against.  That is a practice I will

                 continue to be opposed to.  So it is not for

                 any other reason because I am sure he is a

                 very qualified candidate, but for that reason

                 only, because of this situation with a pension

                 and a salary at state expense that I will be

                 voting in the negative on this nomination.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Volker.

                            SENATOR VOLKER:    Madam President,

                 let me just say that as a former chairman of





                                                          1639



                 the Energy Committee and someone who has had a

                 keen interest in energy for many, many years

                 and dealt with the staff at the Public Service

                 Commission, I, because of my knowledge of the

                 Judge's integrity and intelligence, I would

                 have to say that this is a nomination at this

                 junction in the energy area when, in fact,

                 Senator Wright, who is now the chairman knows

                 very well that we are embarking on an era when

                 energy is going to once again become a major

                 issue, I think not only the state scene, but

                 on the national scene.

                            When someone of the caliber of

                 Leonard Weiss is nominated to the Commission

                 it seems to me that we must say that this is a

                 very outstanding addition to the Public

                 Service Commission, someone who has not only

                 the background, the knowledge of the law, but

                 also I think understands the problems of the

                 ordinary people and understands the problems

                 that people face not only in businesses but in

                 residential energy costs.

                            I must admit that I may be a little

                 biased since I have known Leonard Weiss for

                 over 20 years.  He has been a personal friend





                                                          1640



                 and advisor at times.  We have even referred

                 some law practice back and forth at times over

                 the years.  So I'm not without some bias, but

                 I can truly say that he is a fine gentleman

                 and one of the most brilliant people I have

                 ever met.  And I think he will make an

                 excellent addition to the Public Service

                 Commission, and I think the Governor should be

                 commended.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The question is

                 on the confirmation of Leonard A. Weiss as a

                 member of the Public Service Commission.

                 practicing law on State Street here in Albany

                 and also as a judge both in the Supreme Court

                 and Appellate Division and I have the utmost





                                                          1641



                 personal regard both for his integrity,

                 intelligence, professionalism.  As President

                 of the Senate, Judge Weiss, I congratulate you

                 and am very honored to be here as a part of

                 this process today.

                            (Applause.)

                            THE SECRETARY:    As a member of

                 the State Commission of Correction, Alan J.

                 Croce of Mattituck.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator LaValle.

                            SENATOR LAVALLE:    Madam





                                                          1643



                 President, I rise to move the nomination of

                 Alan J. Croce as a member of the State

                 Commission on Corrections.

                            I would like to say that the

                 Governor should be congratulated once again

                 for this reappointment of Alan Croce to the

                 Board.

                            Mr. Croce has a resume that I

                 believe speaks very highly of his

                 qualifications and the skills that he brings

                 to this position.  More than 28 years in law

                 enforcement.  But probably what is equally as

                 important to the skills and the background

                 that he brings to this position is the

                 commitment that he has demonstrated in the

                 last two years as Chairman of the Commission

                 on Corrections.

                            Mr. Croce has probably, in the last

                 two years traveled more miles visiting the

                 corrections facilities to make sure that

                 people were being properly served and that the

                 system was working correctly.

                            And so it is with great pleasure

                 that I rise to move his nomination.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Nozzolio.





                                                          1644



                            SENATOR NOZZOLIO:    Thank you,

                 Madam President.

                            My colleagues, I wish to echo the

                 comments of Senator LaValle in praising

                 Governor Pataki for making this nomination.

                            During the last few years I have

                 had the honor of chairing the Crime Victims

                 Crime and Corrections Committee of this great

                 body and can tell you that Commissioner Croce

                 has done an outstanding job in working through

                 the correctional system at the local level in

                 conjunction and coordination with the State

                 correctional system and has been a true, true

                 guiding light in a very, very turbulent time

                 for our correctional system in this State.

                            Commissioner Croce is direct.  He

                 is concise and he has been extremely helpful

                 to all levels of government as we wrestle with

                 very important correctional issues.

                            Senator LaValle said it best but I

                 do want to repeat it, that we are truly

                 blessed with this nomination.  The corrections

                 system at this time needs a leadership and I

                 am very pleased that Alan Croce has decided to

                 continue in this very important capacity and





                                                          1645



                 Governor Pataki has recognized the wonderful

                 work that Commissioner Croce has done in

                 guiding our corrections system through what we

                 hope will be a very improved system in the

                 years ahead.

                            Commissioner Croce, my hat is off

                 to you.  You have done an absolutely

                 outstanding job for the people of this state

                 and I am honored to commend you here on this

                 floor for this very important position.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Maziarz.

                            SENATOR MAZIARZ:    Thank you, very

                 much, Madam President.

                            I,  too, want to join with my

                 colleagues Senator LaValle and Senator

                 Nozzolio and second this nomination by

                 Governor Pataki of Commissioner Croce for

                 reappointment to the Commission on

                 Corrections.

                            I have had the pleasure of dealing

                 with Commission Croce on a number of issues

                 regarding the facilities in some of the

                 smaller upstate counties and it did not make

                 any difference whether it was a small village,

                 town or county facility, Commissioner Croce





                                                          1646



                 always made himself available personally to

                 the sheriffs of those counties and I know that

                 they very much appreciated that.  And I very

                 much appreciated it also and I congratulate

                 Governor Pataki on a fine nomination.

                            Thank you, Madam President.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Senator Maltese.

                            SENATOR MALTESE:    Madam

                 President, I rise to second the nomination so

                 ably made by my good colleagues.

                            As a former chairman of Crime

                 Victims, Crime and Correction, I, quite

                 frankly, was so pleased when Alan Croce was

                 appointed by the Governor.  And this

                 reappointment simply reaffirms an excellent

                 choice made in the first place.  I think it is

                 especially note worthy when someone rises

                 through the ranks, if you will, and the people

                 that work on the job in the correctional

                 facilities know that somebody that understands

                 their problems is now making decisions that

                 effect their daily lives and the daily lives

                 of the persons that work in certainly one of

                 the most difficult jobs in the country.

                            So I not only commend the Governor





                                                          1647



                 on this excellent appointment, but personally

                 commend Alan Croce for the sacrifice and

                 dedication that he has shown in undertaking

                 these arduous duties and doing them so very,

                 very well.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The question is

                 on the confirmation.

                            Senator Waldon, go ahead, Senator.

                            SENATOR WALDON:    Madam President,

                 would you recognize me, please.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Absolutely.

                            SENATOR WALDON:    To second the

                 nomination.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    Go ahead.

                            SENATOR WALDON:    I apologize for

                 the lateness of my standing, Madam President,

                 but I did not realize I had met Mr. Croce

                 before, I did not realize that he was here,

                 because I didn't look at the calendar.  And I

                 don't really know too much about his law

                 enforcement experience though I know he is

                 from a law enforcement background and is

                 highly respected in that regard.

                            But I want to speak about his

                 intelligence.  His wife, the Assemblywoman is





                                                          1648



                 here,  please stand up Assemblywoman, to let

                 these people know how smart your husband is.

                 Any man that intelligent to marry a woman so

                 beautiful we should confirm him right away and

                 congratulate him and send him to do the work

                 of the Governor.

                            Thank you.

                            THE PRESIDENT:    The question is
